claims.text: Cheap: one interpreter start, ~0.3 s, against a suite run of seconds to minutes.
claims.why: No timing code is present in this chunk to verify the performance claim.

claims.text: Reports rather than asserts, so the caller decides. A probe that exited non-zero on mismatch would be indistinguishable from a probe that failed to start, which is the distinction this whole module is about.
claims.why: PROBE_SOURCE prints JSON and does not call sys.exit; it reports results. The comment's reasoning about indistinguishability is consistent with the code.

claims.text: Deliberately says "evaluation" and never "candidate": the candidate has not been judged, and a reader must not be able to mistake this for a bad score.
claims.why: as_error() returns a string starting with 'EVALUATION VOID (not a candidate failure)'.

claims.text: FAIL-CLOSED in every direction. A probe that will not start, times out, returns unparseable output, or cannot import daedalus at all reports ok=False -- because 'we could not establish which tree would be scored' and 'the wrong tree would be scored' have the same consequence for a promotion decision, and neither is a green light.
claims.why: The function body is incomplete in this chunk (truncated at subprocess.run), so the fail-closed logic is not yet implemented. The claim refers to behavior not fully present.

observations.what: check_import_provenance is truncated mid-function; the subprocess.run call is incomplete and no return value or error handling is shown.
PROBE_SOURCE uses a try/except to catch import errors and includes them in the JSON output, consistent with the 'reports rather than asserts' design.
The docstring historical narrative (ADR-015, 2026 dates) contains claims about past bugs and fixes that cannot be verified from this code alone.
